drhp.business: The Company operates in the hospitality sector, providing food and beverages and accommodation services to customers. It reports as a single segment covering its hotel units. It serves leisure, business and 'bleisure' travellers in the Indian market and holds one wholly owned subsidiary, Super Civiltech Private Limited.

drhp.expansion: The annual report discloses no narrative expansion or capacity-addition programme. The only expansion-related item is a land purchase: the capital-commitments disclosure records advances paid towards the purchase of a plot, with a balance capital commitment still outstanding against that purchase as at 31 March 2026. Other estimated capital commitments not provided for were Nil at the year end.

risks.note: Management explicitly flags that the risk of business slowdown, inadequate growth and negative returns has increased, calling hospitality 'the most affected' industry; its readiness plan (next-generation talent models, data-driven decision making, customer loyalty, operational flexibility) is still, in its own words, awaiting 'the path from theory to action'.

A security breach would require notifying past and present guests, is costly, damages the brand, and can expose the Company to liability claims for failure to protect data — a risk rising as more hospitality systems are digitised.
risks.risk: Cyber security and guest data privacy

risks.note: Guests are described as potentially the biggest direct and indirect threat to profitability; lawsuits from injured persons and damage to guestrooms are a stated risk to the bottom line, mitigated only through internal controls and closer management of property.

Maintaining high and consistent standards is described as challenging due to the geographical distance separating each establishment; any infringement by an inferior brand may affect customers' perception, requiring registered IP rights and regular IP audits.
risks.risk: Brand protection and consistency across dispersed units

risks.note: Cost pressures related to manpower, energy and food inflation remained key considerations for operators during the year, and rising operational costs are named a continuing challenge — direct margin exposure for a single-segment hotel and F&B business.
risks.risk: Cost inflation in manpower, energy and food

risks.note: Inflationary pressures across major economies, geopolitical uncertainties and currency volatility — particularly a relatively strong US dollar — continued to impact international travel demand and inbound tourism flows in select markets.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic, geopolitical and currency volatility affecting travel demand

risks.note: Regional airline capacity remained approximately 8%-12% below pre-pandemic (2019) levels during FY 2025-26, capping international travel volumes until fleet expansion and route additions narrow the gap.

Rapidly changing customer demands and a boom in guest-facing connected technologies are named as factors changing the sector's risk landscape; without digital and online-marketing capability management says it is increasingly difficult to build a profitable hotel business model.
risks.risk: Rapidly changing guest expectations and technology adoption

sk.overview: The overnight ocean and coastal cruise industry in India is a nascent, high-growth segment of cruise tourism.
